en.html:
The weather overhead was changing. Dramatically.

The besieging army had seemed unstoppable. Any moment now they would break into the castle. Then one airship appeared in the northeast...
Almost instantly it swept aside the occupation dragoons sent to intercept it and advanced over Fudaraku.

Under that extraordinary pressure, the occupation fleet began pulling back.
Even the Galley Keep wasn't trying to counterattack. Perhaps it meant to watch for a while first. With dragoons guarding it, the great ship turned away.

en.html:
A magnificent ship, certainly.
Even from far away I could see the excellence of its design. Not merely make it enormous and declare success.

Bada hai, therefore good hai. A tempting principle. Apply it to a sword and soon four men must carry it to the enemy, who can leave while they are turning the corner. Apply it to a shoe and the soldier can live inside, but marching becomes a housing problem. There had to be some point at which a designer said enough. This ship appeared to have reached that point without first needing somebody to explain the shoe.

Probably one of the strongest airships in the world at present.

en.html:
The fighting power of the units it carried was extraordinary.

That aerial engagement just now...
It had happened too high above us for me to make out the details. But that was sniping.

Matenkou's units were shooting down enemy armor from long range.
Those mounted guns were not HVAP, the high-velocity armor-piercing weapons generally considered the most promising next generation of ADSA—ranged weapons against armored warriors.

Too much accuracy. Too much power. HVAP could not explain it.
Something else. Newer, and more terrible...

Chachamaru pointed upward. Fighting had started again.

Fighting, if we could call it that.
Sasagawa's Zero-Zero units had latched onto the occupation dragoons left as the rear guard. They wouldn't let the enemy anywhere near them. From far away they simply fired, and down the enemy went. All one-sided.

Less a battle than a hunt.
To be accurate about it, a hunt for sport.

en.html:
A miserable sight.

The British Empire's knights drew swords, leveled spears, and charged bravely. Proper courage, proper skill, everything a warrior was supposed to bring. Then somebody far away fired, and all those qualifications fell out of the sky together.

Not even one cut could they give in return. Arre, at least let the man reach you before making his whole life obsolete. No. The new age was not waiting for a sword fight to finish. It had brought a cannon precisely to avoid having one.

The sniper fire seemed almost to mock them. So easily they were struck down, their deaths achieving nothing.

For that instant I felt with them. Not with the allies who had pulled us out of danger. With our enemies.

Time had moved on and left them standing there, weapons ready for a world that had stopped existing. That sorrow, I shared.

ja.html:
無惨な光景であった。

　剣を抜き、槍を構え、勇壮にも突進する大英帝国の
騎士たちは――わずか一太刀を報いる事さえ叶わない。
　嘲笑じみた狙撃を浴び、いとも容易く打ち倒され、
虚しくも死に絶えてゆく。

　その一瞬、俺は窮地を救ってくれた友軍ではなく、
敵である彼らの側に同調した。
　時の流れに置き捨てられた者の悲哀を共有した。

Kageaki"So the age is changing."
Chachamaru"The League's army is improving its HVAP too. They'll have it in combat soon."
Chachamaru"Stand far apart and bang-bang at each other. That'll be the whole of war. The dance of blades will disappear from the battlefield."
Kageaki"..."
Chachamaru"You can't make a myth in an age like that."
Chachamaru"No heroes, no demon kings. Even God probably won't find a gap to crawl out through."
Chachamaru"That's why we do it now, bhai. While we still can."
Kageaki"Call God..."
Chachamaru"At the end of the old age. Make the final myth."
Chachamaru"Well, just squeezing in before the door shuts, I suppose..."

Outside the castle, too, the occupation army had begun withdrawing.

Much of its offensive had depended on superiority in the air. Bombing support, in other words.
Now that was gone. Naturally they would have to reconsider their operations.

It seemed we could gain some time.
The time we needed. Until Hikaru woke.
